action: press 'Up' -- move the selection off the ready-made characters and onto the one I fill in myself
commentary: There is a rack of people already made up in here and I am not any of them. Up one, to the one where I answer the questions myself.

action: press 'Return' -- take the entry that lets me fill myself in by hand
commentary: Right. Let us see what I look like written down.

action: press 'f' -- finish the world settings as the engine offered them
commentary: Fairport Harbor. I have run gear out of a dozen towns with a name like that. I did not pick this world, I only woke up in it, so I will take it as it stands.

action: press 'Y' -- answer the case-sensitive confirmation with the capital it wants
commentary: Yes. I am finished deciding about the shape of the world. Nothing about it is mine to argue with.

action: press 'shift+Tab' -- step back to the points page before I choose anything about myself
commentary: Before I answer anything I want to see what the answers cost. Show me the ledger first.

action: press 'Down' -- move down off the no-limits budget onto the one with separate pools
commentary: A version of me with no limits is not a person, it is a wish. Down one.

action: press 'Return' -- take the budget where every gain has to be paid for somewhere else
commentary: That is how it has always worked. If I am strong in one place I am paying for it in another, and I would rather see the bill than pretend there is not one.

action: press 'Tab' -- move on to where this starts
commentary: Right. Now where does this begin.

action: press 'slash' -- open the search on the list of starts
commentary: There is a long list here and I already know which one is mine.

action: press 'm' -- begin spelling the start I am looking for
commentary: M.

action: press 'i' -- keep spelling it
commentary: I.

action: press 's' -- finish spelling it
commentary: S. Missed. That is the honest word for what happened to me.

action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what is left of the list
commentary: Show me what is left when I ask for that.

action: press 'Return' -- take the start that matches what actually happened to me
commentary: I did not get out. I was on the water when it started and I came back to a harbour nobody was managing any more, so this is the honest one to take.

action: press 'Tab' -- move on to what I actually am
commentary: That is settled then. Now the trade.

action: press 'slash' -- open the search on the trades
commentary: I know the answer to this one without reading the list.

action: press 'f' -- begin spelling my trade
commentary: F.

action: press 'i' -- keep spelling it
commentary: I.

action: press 's' -- keep spelling it
commentary: S.

action: press 'h' -- finish spelling it
commentary: H. Fisher. Thirty-one seasons of it.

action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what is left
commentary: Show me.

action: press 'Return' -- take the trade I actually have
commentary: Thirty-one seasons. A rod, a knife on my hip, waders, and my father's wrist watch, which is the only thing on that list I would fight to keep.

action: press 'Tab' -- move on from the trade
commentary: That is me on paper. What else do they want.

action: press 'slash' -- open the search on the other things I am
commentary: There are two habits I am not going to pretend about, and they are both on this page.

action: press 'n' -- begin spelling the first of them
commentary: N.

action: press 'i' -- keep spelling it
commentary: I.

action: press 'c' -- finish spelling it
commentary: C. Nicotine. Since I was nineteen.

action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what is left
commentary: Show me.

action: press 'Return' -- take the habit I have had since I was nineteen
commentary: I have smoked since I was nineteen and I am not going to stand here and pretend it is under control. It earns me a point and it will cost me a headache when the cigarettes run out.

action: press 'slash' -- open the search again for the other habit
commentary: And the other one.

action: press 'c' -- begin spelling it
commentary: C.

action: press 'a' -- keep spelling it
commentary: A.

action: press 'f' -- keep spelling it
commentary: F.

action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see the two that match
commentary: Show me both of them.

action: press 'Down' -- move off the extreme version of it onto the plain one
commentary: No. I drink it black and I drink a lot of it, but I have never gone strange from it. The one under it.

action: press 'Return' -- take the plain coffee habit
commentary: Black, and too much of it, for thirty-odd years. When it runs out I will have a head like a bell for two days and then I will be fine.

action: press 'slash' -- open the search once more, to take something off the list
commentary: There is one on there that is not true of me.

action: press 'BackSpace' -- rub out the old search; nothing on the screen changed
commentary: Clear that out first.

action: press 'h' -- type over the selected search text instead of trying to rub it out
commentary: H. Over the top of it, then.

action: press 'i' -- keep spelling it
commentary: I.

action: press 'g' -- finish spelling it
commentary: G. High school.

action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what it found
commentary: Show me.

action: press 'Return' -- take the schooling back off the list, because I never had it
commentary: I left school at sixteen for the boats. I have felt the lack of it my whole life and I am not going to write myself a diploma now to make the page look better.

action: press 'slash' -- open the search for the one piece of paper I do have
commentary: There is one licence on that list I have actually held in my hand.

action: press 'b' -- type over what the box is holding
commentary: B.

action: press 'o' -- keep spelling it
commentary: O.

action: press 'a' -- finish spelling it
commentary: A. Boating.

action: press 'Return' -- close the search
commentary: Show me.

action: press 'Return' -- take the boating licence, because I have held one for nine years
commentary: Nine years with my own boat under me. Forty-two feet of nineteen seventies fiberglass and a diesel I rebuilt twice with my own hands. It costs nothing to say so and it is the truest line here.

action: press 'Tab' -- move on to the honest part
commentary: Now the part where I put a number on myself.

action: press 'plus' -- put strength up where it belongs
commentary: Thirty-one years of hauling traps over a gunwale. This is the one thing on this page nobody who has seen me work would argue with.

action: press 'plus' -- and once more
commentary: I can still put a full trap on the rail without thinking about it. Ten, and that is the top of what I will claim.

action: press 'Down' -- move down past the hands
commentary: My hands are ordinary. I have never been quick, only steady, and steady is not on this list.

action: press 'Down' -- and down again, to the schooling I never had
commentary: Here is where I pay for the boats.

action: press 'minus' -- take a point off the book-learning, which I never had
commentary: I left school at sixteen for the boats and I have felt the lack of it ever since. Anything that comes out of a book comes to me slowly and I would rather say so than pretend.

action: press 'Down' -- move down to what I got instead
commentary: And here is what I got instead of schooling.

action: press 'plus' -- put my eyes up where they actually are
commentary: I can read a change in the water at half a mile. It is the only talent I would ever claim out loud.

action: press 'plus' -- and once more, and that is the last of it
commentary: I notice things before I have decided to. Ten, and I will not gild it past that.

action: press 'Tab' -- move on to what is wrong with me, and what is right
commentary: Now the part I have been putting off. I would rather know my own weight than flatter myself.

action: press 'slash' -- open the search on the list of what I am
commentary: Start with the thing that will put me on the floor.

action: press 'b' -- begin spelling the first honest thing
commentary: B.

action: press 'a' -- keep spelling it
commentary: A.

action: press 'c' -- keep spelling it
commentary: C.

action: press 'k' -- finish spelling it
commentary: K. My back.

action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see it written down
commentary: There it is, in a list, like a diagnosis.

action: press 'Return' -- take the back, because it is the truest thing about me
commentary: Six years of it. There is a way of lifting with a twist that will put me on the deck, and I know exactly what it is, and I still do it when I am tired.

action: press 'slash' -- open the search again
commentary: And the other thing I have always known about myself.

action: press 's' -- type over the old search
commentary: S.

action: press 'l' -- keep spelling it
commentary: L.

action: press 'e' -- keep spelling it
commentary: E.

action: press 'e' -- keep spelling it
commentary: E again.

action: press 'p' -- finish spelling it
commentary: P. How I sleep.

action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what it found
commentary: Show me.

action: press 'Return' -- take the sleeping, which was a mercy on the boat and will not be one now
commentary: I slept in a bunk over a running diesel for thirty-one years. I have never once woken up to a noise, and out here that is going to be a problem.

action: press 'slash' -- open the search once more
commentary: One more honest thing, and then the other column.

action: press 'a' -- type over the old search
commentary: A.

action: press 'd' -- keep spelling it
commentary: D.

action: press 'd' -- keep spelling it
commentary: D again.

action: press 'i' -- keep spelling it
commentary: I.

action: press 'c' -- keep spelling it
commentary: C.

action: press 't' -- finish spelling it
commentary: T. It runs straight down my mother's side of the family.

action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what it found
commentary: Show me.

action: press 'Down' -- move off the resistant one, which I am plainly not
commentary: That is the wrong way round. I am not the resistant kind and never have been.

action: press 'Return' -- take the streak that runs in my family
commentary: The boats ran on coffee and cigarettes and I have never pretended either was under control. It cost me one thing I loved already and I am not going to write it out of me now.

action: press 'slash' -- open the search for the other column
commentary: Now the things that are right with me. There are fewer of them and I will not pad the list.

action: press 't' -- type over the old search
commentary: T.

action: press 'o' -- keep spelling it
commentary: O.

action: press 'u' -- keep spelling it
commentary: U.

action: press 'g' -- keep spelling it
commentary: G.

action: press 'h' -- finish spelling it
commentary: H. I do not break easily.

action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what it found
commentary: Show me.

action: press 'Return' -- take the toughness, which is thirty-one seasons and not a gift
commentary: I have been thrown against a gunwale in a February swell and gone back to work the same afternoon. That is not courage, it is just what I am built out of.

action: press 'slash' -- open the search again
commentary: Next.

action: press 's' -- type over the old search
commentary: S.

action: press 't' -- keep spelling it
commentary: T.

action: press 'o' -- keep spelling it
commentary: O.

action: press 'm' -- finish spelling it
commentary: M. My stomach.

action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what it found
commentary: Show me.

action: press 'Up' -- move up off the weak one
commentary: No. The opposite of that, in fact.

action: press 'Up' -- and up again, to the one that is true
commentary: There. That one.

action: press 'Return' -- take the stomach that has never once betrayed me
commentary: I have eaten what was available my whole working life -- bait-box sandwiches, three-day chowder, whatever was in the galley -- and it has never once come back up on me.

action: press 'slash' -- open the search for the last of them
commentary: One more, and it is the one people always get wrong about me.

action: press 'p' -- type over the old search
commentary: P.

action: press 'a' -- keep spelling it
commentary: A.

action: press 'c' -- keep spelling it
commentary: C.

action: press 'k' -- finish spelling it
commentary: K. What I can carry.

action: press 'Return' -- close the search and see what it found
commentary: Show me.

action: press 'Return' -- take the packing, which is a lifetime of stowing gear in a small boat
commentary: Everything on a forty-two foot boat has one place it goes and one way it goes there. My back will still make me pay for the weight, but I know how to stow it.

action: press 'Tab' -- move on to what I can actually do
commentary: That is the whole of what I am. Now what I can do with it.

action: press 'Down' -- start down the list of things a person can be good at
commentary: Bashing things with a stick is not a trade. Past it.

action: press 'Down' -- down again, onto getting out of the way
commentary: Knives are for fish and rope. Here is the one that has actually kept me alive.

action: press 'plus' -- buy the getting out of the way
commentary: Thirty-one seasons teaches you that the sea does not care how much you want to be finished, and that what kills people out there is being in a rush. I do not fight things. I step aside and let them go past.

action: press 'Down' -- keep going down, past the fighting
commentary: Dodging reads two now. Past the hand-to-hand.

action: press 'Down' -- past the spears as well
commentary: Nor that.

action: press 'Down' -- and past fighting with my hands
commentary: I have never hit anybody in my life and I am not going to start claiming I know how.

action: press 'Down' -- past the bows
commentary: The bar is on unarmed now. No.

action: press 'Down' -- past the handguns
commentary: Archery. My father would have laughed.

action: press 'Down' -- past the pistols
commentary: There was a flare pistol in the locker and that is the whole of my education in firearms.

action: press 'Down' -- past whatever a launcher is
commentary: Launchers. I would not know which end to hold.

action: press 'Down' -- past the marksmanship
commentary: Marksmanship. No.

action: press 'Down' -- past the rifles
commentary: Rifles. No.

action: press 'Down' -- past the shotguns
commentary: A man two slips down from me kept one on his boat. I thought it was a foolish thing to have on the water.

action: press 'Down' -- past the machine guns
commentary: Whatever a submachine gun is, it is not mine.

action: press 'Down' -- past the throwing
commentary: I can throw a line. That is not the same thing and I will not pretend it is.

action: press 'Down' -- past the science
commentary: Applied science. That is for people who stayed in school.

action: press 'Down' -- past the wiring
commentary: I can rewire a bilge pump and that is the end of my electrics.

action: press 'plus' -- buy the mending
commentary: Nets, line, canvas, a hull that was half rotten when I bought her. Two years of evenings with resin on my hands and she was sound. This one I have earned.

action: press 'Down' -- move on to the cooking
commentary: Fabrication reads two of mine on top of the one I already had. Next.

action: press 'plus' -- buy the cooking
commentary: Whatever came up in the net, in a pan, with what was in the galley. I have fed a two-person crew on that for nine years and nobody ever complained twice.

action: press 'Down' -- move on down the page
commentary: Food handling is bought. On.

action: press 'Down' -- past the survival, which the trade already gave me
commentary: Five of it came with the trade and that is already more than I would claim. I am not going to buy more of what I have.

action: press 'plus' -- buy the needlework
commentary: Every stitch in my own oilskins is mine. A boat is held together by whoever on board can sew, and on the Marie-Ange that was me.

action: press 'Down' -- on to the swimming
commentary: Tailoring is bought. Next.

action: press 'plus' -- buy the swimming and the wind
commentary: Twice over the side in nine years and twice back aboard, in water that stops your heart if you let it. I am fifty-two and I have no wind for running, but I can still get myself out of the water.

action: press 'Down' -- on down past the computers
commentary: Athletics reads two and two. Two things left that I have actually done.

action: press 'Down' -- and past whatever devices are
commentary: A telephone is a telephone. I do not need a level in it.

action: press 'Down' -- on to the patching-up
commentary: Devices, whatever that means. Past it.

action: press 'plus' -- buy the patching-up
commentary: Fish hooks through a hand, rope burn, a boom to the head, a man with two fingers off. Thirty-one seasons of getting people to the dock in one piece, mostly.

action: press 'Down' -- on to the last one
commentary: Health care is bought. One thing left, and it is the one I am proudest of.

action: press 'plus' -- buy the diesel work
commentary: I rebuilt that diesel twice with my own hands and a manual I could barely read, and she started every morning of the last four seasons. If I can hear a bad bearing I can usually fix it.

action: press 'at' -- put right what it has me down as
commentary: It has me down as a man. I am a woman, fifty-two years of it, and thirty-one of those on a deck where that was the first thing anybody noticed and the last thing that mattered.

action: press 'dollar' -- and dress me accordingly
commentary: And put me in my own clothes while it is at it.

action: press 'a' -- ask it how old I am
commentary: Fifty-two years, and most of them wet.

action: press '5' -- type over the number it guessed
commentary: Five.

action: press '2' -- finish the number
commentary: Two. Fifty-two.

action: press 'Return' -- set my age down
commentary: Fifty-two. Thirty-one seasons out of Gloucester and nine of them on my own boat.

action: press 'n' -- ask it what to call me
commentary: They ought to know what to call me.

action: press 'O' -- begin my given name
commentary: O.

action: press 'd' -- keep spelling it
commentary: D.

action: press 'e' -- keep spelling it
commentary: E.

action: press 't' -- keep spelling it
commentary: T.

action: press 't' -- keep spelling it
commentary: T again.

action: press 'e' -- finish my given name
commentary: E. Odette. Everyone who ever mattered called me Dette.

action: press 'space' -- leave a gap before my father's name; nothing on the screen changed
commentary: And his name after mine.

action: press 'V' -- begin the family name
commentary: V.

action: press 'a' -- keep spelling it
commentary: A.

action: press 'c' -- keep spelling it
commentary: C.

action: press 'h' -- keep spelling it
commentary: H.

action: press 'o' -- keep spelling it
commentary: O.

action: press 'n' -- finish the family name
commentary: N. Vachon. My grandfather brought it down from Riviere-du-Loup in a duffel bag.

action: press 'Return' -- set my name down
commentary: Odette Vachon. Out of Gloucester, and before that out of a duffel bag from Riviere-du-Loup.

action: press 'Tab' -- look over the whole of it before I say yes to it
commentary: Let me see all of it laid out before I sign my name to it.

action: press 'Tab' -- say that this is the whole of me
commentary: Strength ten, hands ordinary, schooling seven, eyes ten. Fifty-two years, five foot nine, A positive. Packmule, strong stomach, tough; addictive, bad back, sleeps like the dead. Survival five, athletics four, and not one weapon on the whole page. That is me, and nothing left over.

action: press 'Y' -- answer the case-sensitive question with the capital it wants
commentary: Yes. Salem is thirty-one miles down the coast and Camille teaches fourth grade in it, and I am not going to find that out from this side of a door.

action: press 'V' -- find out what is in here with me before I move a foot
commentary: Thirty-one seasons taught me to look before I step, and the first thing I want to know in a strange room is whether anything in it is looking back.

action: press 'Escape' -- close the list, having got my answer
commentary: Nothing alive in here but me. That is the best news I am likely to get today, so I will take it and stop looking at golf caps.

action: press 'm' -- look at the chart and find out where in the world I have washed up
commentary: Thirty-one years of reading charts before leaving a mooring. The first thing I want is where the water is.

action: press 'Escape' -- close the chart
commentary: West Rutland. There is not a drop of salt water on this chart, and no coast on it anywhere. Whatever put me here, it put me a long way inland, and Salem might as well be on the moon.

action: press 'bar' -- stand still and listen before I touch anything
commentary: Sit tight and listen. That is most of what fishing ever was, and it has never once been the wrong first move.

action: press 'w' -- choose to wait rather than set the alarm
commentary: My father's watch has an alarm in it and I have not needed one since he died. Waiting is what I want.

action: press '3' -- wait five minutes and listen to the building
commentary: Five minutes. If something in here has heard me it will make itself known in five minutes, and if it has not then I can start moving about like a person instead of a burglar.

action: press 'Y' -- stop the wait, because that sound is worth answering
commentary: Gargling. That is not a gull and it is not wind in a gutter -- that is a throat that does not work any more, and it is close enough that I heard it through a wall. I stop resting. I would rather know where it is standing than get my five minutes.

action: press 'V' -- take a sounding: find out whether the thing to the northwest can be seen from here
commentary: Northwest, the log says, and northwest of me is a shut door. Before I move I want to know whether it is in the room with me or behind that door. On the water you never guess at a shape in the fog; you take a sounding and then you decide.

action: press 'Tab' -- turn the list from goods to living things
commentary: Golf caps, golf balls, a till with fifteen dollars in it that nobody will ever want again, and a stick fifty-one paces southeast. None of that is what I asked. I want the other column: what is breathing.

action: press 'Tab' -- turn the list again, to what the building is made of
commentary: Nothing. Not one living shape on the whole page, and I heard it plain. So it is behind a wall and it has not seen me, and that is the best news I have had since I woke up. Now let me see what this place is built out of, because I need water before I need anything else.

action: press 'Escape' -- close the survey, having learned the thing I did not want to learn
commentary: Twenty-six display racks, six counters, three desks, eight windows, a broken vending machine, two trash cans -- and not one tap, not one basin, not one cistern in the whole building. A shop for golfers. Of course there is no water in it. Outside there is grass and pavement, a cottonwood, nannyberry, hobblebush and rose. That is my larder and it is thin.

action: press 'Right' -- walk east off the open carpet, toward the goods and away from the shut door I heard through
commentary: First thing: get off this carpet. It is the middle of a dark room with a door at my shoulder and whatever made that noise on the other side of it. I go east, toward the light and the racks, and I put furniture between us.

action: press 'Right' -- keep going east, off the carpet and onto the shop floor
commentary: One step and I have already made noise -- five, the readout says, and that is walking softly in waders. Nothing to do about that. Keep going.

action: press 'Right' -- one more step east, to stand alongside the racks
commentary: The racks are two deep along this row and I can see cloth hanging on the one below me. I stop beside them rather than walking into them. Nothing in a shop is worth barging.

action: press 'g' -- reach for what is on the rack beside me instead of walking into it
commentary: Cloth on a rack, and I am a woman in a tank top and waders with a shut door somewhere behind me and nothing on my arms. I will take whatever is hanging there if it will cover skin. That is not vanity, that is the difference between a scratch and a bite.

action: press 'greater' -- open the bag up before deciding whether to carry it; nothing on the screen changed
commentary: A golf bag on the rack one step southeast. A bag is a bag and I could use one, but a bag is also whatever is standing in it, and what I want standing in it is something with weight at the far end. Let me look inside before I heave it onto a back that will make me pay for it.

action: press 'W' -- put the empty bag on rather than carry it in my hands
commentary: Empty, then. No club, no umbrella, nothing. But it is a big soft bag with a strap and I have a fish trap, fifteen baits and a lighter to my name, so I will take the space and be glad of it. Over the shoulder, not in the hands. My hands are for the rod and the knife.

action: press 'Up' -- work north up the aisle toward the counter and the desks
commentary: Four pounds heavier and I can feel the strap already. Now the counter. In any shop worth the name the useful things are behind the counter, not on the racks, and there are three desks in this building according to my own eyes.

action: press 'Up' -- keep north along the open floor beside the racks
commentary: Quiet as I can go in waders. The floorboards here are wood over something hollow and every step tells the room where I am. Nothing I can do about that either, so I go steadily and I listen between steps.

action: press 'Up' -- north again, two paces off the counter now
commentary: Two seconds that step cost me instead of one. Something underfoot, or the bag catching. I will learn this floor by the end of the day whether I want to or not.

action: press 'Up' -- one more north, up level with the counter
commentary: There is the counter, and the till standing open on it with fifteen dollars in the drawer. Fifteen dollars. I would trade the lot for one bottle with a cap on it.

action: press 'g' -- reach across the counter for whatever is lying on it; nothing in the map column changed
commentary: There is something small on the counter within arm's reach, and out through the east windows, sitting on the tarmac between two painted lines, there is a car. A whole car. I have had a licence since I was seventeen and I have never once been so glad of it. But the counter first. One thing at a time, in order, the way you clear a deck.

action: press 'Down' -- turn round and head south down the aisle for the door in the east wall
commentary: Nothing on the counter but the till and fifteen dollars I cannot drink. So: the car. There is a door in the east wall about nine paces south of me and I would rather use a door than a window, because a window costs skin and I have no skin to spare.

action: press 'Down' -- south again
commentary: One pace at a time and the clock ticking one second for each. It is a strange comfort, that. Out on the water you count seconds too, between the flash and the thunder, to know how far off the weather is.

action: press 'Down' -- south past the last of the racks
commentary: There is the green thing still hanging on the rack to my left as I pass. A jacket, maybe. I will come back for it if the day allows. It is not going anywhere and neither, I suspect, is anyone else who might want it.

action: press 'n' -- cut southeast now the racks have run out; nothing in the map column changed
commentary: The racks end here so I can cut the corner. Diagonally, which costs more in the legs but less in time, and my legs are the one thing that still work the way they did at thirty.

action: press 'Down' -- straight south instead, since the rack will not let me cut
commentary: Straight down the aisle then, and no more cleverness. The rack wins that argument.

action: press 'Down' -- south again, past the green garment on the rack
commentary: The green thing on the rack is a jacket after all, hanging on the end of the line. I mark where it is. If I come back inside before dark it is two paces off my way.

action: press 'n' -- try the diagonal again now the racks really have ended
commentary: Now the line has ended for certain, and I will take the corner I was refused a minute ago.

action: press 'n' -- step southeast toward the pale shape standing against the east wall
commentary: There is something pale and squat against the east wall, two along and two down, and from here it could be a bin or it could be a basin. If it is a basin there may be an inch of water still in the trap, and an inch of water is a great deal more than nothing. I go and put my hand on it.

action: press 'e' -- put a hand on the pale shape rather than guess at it from across the room; nothing in the map column changed
commentary: Close enough now to reach it. I will not guess. Guessing is how people drown.

action: press 'Down' -- leave the pale shape alone and drop south toward the door
commentary: Nothing to be had from it. Whatever it is, it is shut up or it is empty, and I have wasted a breath on it. There is no water in a golf shop and I should have known that from the door. Fine. Then it is the car, and it is the bushes, and it is whatever the day gives me.

action: press 'n' -- southeast into the dark corner in front of the door
commentary: There is a patch of dark in front of that door where the daylight from the windows does not reach. I step into it. If anything is going to be standing on the other side of the glass I would rather it did not see me first.

action: press 'o' -- open the door properly instead of shouldering it
commentary: Hand on the handle, not a shoulder. A door you open quietly you can also close quietly, and I intend to come back through this one before dark.

action: press 'Right' -- step into the open doorway and look out before going any further
commentary: Open. It swung without a sound, which is the first kind thing this building has done for me. Now stand in the gap and look, and do not walk out into the middle of a car park like a woman going to fetch the post.

action: press 'Right' -- step out of the doorway onto the sidewalk
commentary: Three of them. Three red cars sitting in a golf club car park with their seats still in them, and not a soul moving anywhere on the tarmac. Whoever parked here on the last morning never came back for them. Nine paces to the near one. I will walk it like I am walking a dock at night: steady, no running, eyes up.

action: press 'n' -- angle southeast across the tarmac toward the near car
commentary: Out in the open now, sun on the back of my neck and nothing between me and the treeline. I do not like it. Southeast, and quickly, and no dawdling in the middle of a car park.

action: press 'n' -- second diagonal southeast
commentary: Tarmac under the waders, which is a sound I will not learn to like. Two more like this and I am at the wing of it.

action: press 'n' -- third diagonal, lining up on the car's flank
commentary: Third one. My back is telling me about the bag already and I have carried nothing in it yet.

action: press 'Right' -- straight east now, at the car's flank
commentary: I can see it properly from here. Four seats in it and the windscreen still whole, doors hanging on both sides, and the boot end pointing at me. That pale thing indoors was a rubbish bin after all, and an empty one. This is better. A car has a boot, and people put things in boots they never think about again.

action: press 'Right' -- east again
commentary: Two seconds a pace out here. Waders were never made for tarmac.

action: press 'Right' -- east once more, over the painted line
commentary: Over the yellow line. Somebody painted this so people would leave a decent gap between wing mirrors. There is nobody left to mind it.

action: press 'g' -- reach into the car for whatever is stowed in it; nothing in the map column changed
commentary: Close enough to put my hand on the paint. Now let us see what a golfer leaves in the back of his car on a Thursday morning in May.

action: press 'Right' -- one more east, right up against the paintwork
commentary: Not close enough after all. There is a painted bay line between me and it and my arm is not that long. One more.

action: press 'e' -- put a hand on the car and see what it will tell me
commentary: Right up on it now. Red paint, warm already where the sun has been on it. Let us find out whether this thing has anything in it besides four seats and somebody's last Thursday.

action: press 'Right' -- answer the direction prompt with east, where the car is
commentary: A squirrel. There is a squirrel somewhere east of me and my mouth actually watered, which tells you everything about the morning I am having. It can wait. It is not going to hold still for a woman in waders anyway. East, into the car.

action: press 'e' -- choose to examine the vehicle rather than just mark where it is
commentary: It offers to let me remember where the car is parked. I know where it is parked. It is parked twenty feet from a shop with no water in it, which is a fact I will not be forgetting. Examine it.

action: press 'Escape' -- close the car down, having learned what it is and what it is not
commentary: A hatchback. Dented, four seats, twenty-one litres of petrol in two tanks and a motor listed faulty with nothing at all in the acceleration line, so it will not turn a wheel for me. The boot is bare. Not a bottle, not a rag, not a road atlas. It offered to let me draw the fuel off and then greyed the offer out, because that wants a length of hose and I have none. What it does have is four dry seats and a hole where a window should be. I will remember both.

action: press 'V' -- survey the ground from out here in the open, where I can see
commentary: Wait. Wait. A golf course. Eighteen greens and every course I have ever driven past has a pond in it somewhere, because rich men like to lose balls in water. And I have a rod in my hand and fifteen baits in my vest. If there is a hazard on this course then I am not a woman with no water, I am a woman with a fishery. Let me look properly from out here where nothing is in the way.

action: press 'Tab' -- turn the survey past the goods
commentary: Goods first, always. I do not want goods. I want a shape of water.

action: press 'Tab' -- and past the living things, to the ground itself
commentary: Not goods. Not the living. The ground. Show me the ground.

action: press 'Tab' -- come back round to the ground and read the rest of it
commentary: One squirrel, fifty-six paces east and running away from me. Good luck to it. But the ground list is fifty-nine things long and I only saw thirty, and among the thirty were eight hundred and fifty tiles of forest floor, a hundred and eighty of underbrush and nine of bamboo shoots. Forest means forage and bamboo shoots you can eat. Let me see the rest.

action: press 'Next' -- page down the ground list to the part I could not see
commentary: Turn the page. If there is water on this course it will be down here somewhere in the far half.

action: press 'Next' -- page down again, further into the far half
commentary: Now I have the distances and they change everything. Forest floor six paces south. Underbrush seven paces south. There is a wood at the bottom of this car park, close enough to spit into, and a wood in May has things in it a woman can eat. Bamboo shoots twenty-two north. Keep turning.

action: press 'Next' -- and again, to the bottom of the list
commentary: Keep going. The far end is where the greens will be, and the greens are where the water will be.

action: press 'Next' -- one more page, to the very bottom
commentary: There they are. Sixty-eight tiles of green and three flags. Basswood, sassafras, oak, pine, hickory, birch, chokeberry, moss. A whole wood and a whole course in front of me and still no water on the list. One more page.

action: press 'Next' -- the last page of the ground
commentary: Willow. Nine willows. Now that is worth more to me than the whole car. Willow does not grow where the ground is dry, it grows with its feet wet, and nine of them together means standing water or ground that thinks it is water. Whoever laid out this course put them somewhere for a reason and the reason will be a pond.

action: press 'Escape' -- close the survey and go to the wood, since the wood is what I can reach
commentary: Fifty-nine kinds of ground in sight and not one drop of water in any of them. So be it. I am not going to walk into a wood I cannot see the far side of chasing willows, not today, not on my own, not with a rod for a weapon. But there is forest floor six paces south of me and a hundred and eighty-four tiles of underbrush behind it, and underbrush in May is greens and shoots and roots. A woman can go a day thirsty. She cannot go a day thirsty and empty.

action: press 'Down' -- south off the tarmac toward the wood
commentary: South. Off the tarmac, over the kerb, into the green.

action: press 'Down' -- south off the tarmac toward the wood
commentary: South. Off the tarmac, over the kerb, into the green.

action: press 'Down' -- south off the tarmac toward the wood
commentary: South. Off the tarmac, over the kerb, into the green.

action: press 'Down' -- over the kerb onto the grass
commentary: The kerb, and then real ground under me for the first time since I woke. Grass with dead patches in it where the mowers stopped in April and nobody came back. There is a leafy thing four paces down with proper broad leaves on it.

action: press 'Down' -- down onto the grass proper
commentary: Grass. Actual grass. My knees are grateful and my back is not, and both of them are right.

action: press 'Down' -- two more paces to the leafy plant
commentary: Softer underfoot than tarmac and quieter too, which suits me. Two more and I can get my hands into it.

action: press 'Down' -- up alongside the plant
commentary: Grass takes two seconds a pace where tarmac took one. It is thicker than it looks from a car park.

action: press 'e' -- get my hands into the underbrush and search it
commentary: I am standing in it. Broad leaves round my boots and the log telling me it is slow going, which it always is. Thirty-one seasons of picking things out of nets with cold hands and I can tell you that the difference between a full belly and an empty one is nearly always patience. So: down on my haunches, and search it properly.

action: press 'Y' -- answer yes and forage the underbrush
commentary: Yes. Yes, of course yes.

action: press 'g' -- gather up what the underbrush gave me
commentary: Two handfuls of young leaves, fresh. That is not a meal but it is greens and greens hold water, and water is the thing I have not got. Six seconds it took me. I would have spent six hours.

action: press 'a' -- mark the leaves so I can take them
commentary: There they are, listed as mine to take. Mark them.

action: press 'Return' -- confirm and take the leaves
commentary: Marked. Take them.

action: press 'n' -- southeast, toward the next patch of broad leaves
commentary: In my vest. Now, two handfuls is not a day's eating for a woman my size, and the patch I just stripped is bare stalks. There is another one with proper leaves on it six along and two down, at the edge where the grass gives out onto the road. Two handfuls at a time is how you fill a hold.

action: press 'n' -- southeast again, down to the road's edge
commentary: Three seconds to get out of it, because getting out of underbrush costs you as much as getting in. Down to the edge and then straight along.

action: press 'Right' -- east along the edge of the grass
commentary: Now east, along the seam where the grass meets the tarmac. Easier walking and I can see both ways at once.

action: press 'Right' -- east again
commentary: Two along. The road below me runs east and west with a painted line down the middle of it and not a car moving on it in either direction.

action: press 'Right' -- east, third pace
commentary: Three. Nearly on it.

action: press 'e' -- search the second patch without stepping into it
commentary: Right beside me now, and I have learned my lesson about wading into the stuff: it costs three seconds to get out again and three seconds is three seconds. I will search it from where I stand.

action: press 'm' -- put the chart up now that I have walked a little of it
commentary: Nothing in that one. That is how it goes; two nets come up full and the third comes up with a boot in it. Before I go back in I want the chart again. I have walked a hundred feet since I last looked at it and a hundred feet is sometimes the difference between a blank sheet and a pond.

action: press 'Up' -- walk the chart north a square at a time and read what each one is called
commentary: There is the course, laid out north of me in green stipple, four squares deep, with my shop and its neighbour at the bottom edge of it. And there, at the top edge, a small round patch of pale blue. Blue on a chart means one thing. I am going to name every square between me and it before I take a single step.

action: press 'Up' -- north again on the chart
commentary: The square above me is the car park itself. Of course it is. Keep going north.

action: press 'Up' -- north onto the course itself
commentary: Car park, then the course. Two squares up and I am on the fairway.

action: press 'Up' -- north again, still on the course
commentary: Still the course. It is a big one.

action: press 'Up' -- one more north, to the pale blue square
commentary: Four squares of golf course. One more and I am on the blue.

action: press 'Left' -- one square west, onto the blue
commentary: Forest trail at the top of the course, which is worth knowing on its own: a trail is a way through a wood without fighting the wood. But the blue is one square to the left of it.

action: press 'N' -- put a mark on the chart where the water is
commentary: Swamp. Swamp, five squares north and one west, and nine willows standing in view to tell me the same thing from ground level. I was right and being right has never felt this good. Now I mark it. You do not carry a bearing in your head for a day and trust it. You write it on the chart.

action: press 'W' -- begin writing the mark
commentary: It even offers me colours for it, which is more courtesy than I have had from anything else today. I do not need a colour. I need five letters that will still mean something to me at first light when I am dry-mouthed and not thinking straight.

action: press 'A' -- second letter
commentary: W. A woman writing on a chart with one finger, like my father did.

action: press 'T' -- third letter
commentary: W, A. He wrote his in pencil so he could rub out a mark when a bank shifted.

action: press 'E' -- fourth letter
commentary: W, A, T.

action: press 'R' -- last letter
commentary: W, A, T, E. One more and it is written down where it cannot fall out of my head.

action: press 'Return' -- set the mark down on the chart
commentary: WATER. Five letters on a swamp five squares north, and now it is on the chart and not in my head, and my head can go back to worrying about tonight.

action: press 'Escape' -- put the chart away and start back for the door
commentary: Written. WATER, in yellow, on a swamp five squares north with a forest trail running down to it. That is tomorrow settled. Today is nearly settled too, because I have nothing to carry water in and I am not walking into a bog on my first evening with a rod and a knife and a bad back. Home, such as it is. There is a door I left open and I want it shut behind me before the light goes.

action: press 'y' -- northwest, back the way I came
commentary: Thirteen paces east and twelve south is how far I have wandered from that door, and every one of them has to be walked back. Northwest, then, on the diagonal, and I will go round the cars rather than through them.

action: press 'y' -- northwest again
commentary: Two seconds a pace on grass. It adds up, and my back is keeping the tally.

action: press 'y' -- northwest, third stride
commentary: Eight minutes past eight and I have already been out, been round a car, been down to the road and back. On the boat that would be a whole morning's work done before the kettle.

action: press 'y' -- northwest onto the kerb
commentary: Up over the kerb next and back onto the hard stuff, which is quick walking and loud walking both.

action: press 'y' -- northwest onto the tarmac, passing west of the car
commentary: The hatchback is straight up the line from me with both its doors hanging open like a gutted fish. I go up the west side of it. Nine west and eight north to that door and the diagonal takes me clear of the paintwork.

action: press 'y' -- northwest again across the lot
commentary: One second a pace on tarmac against two on grass. Whoever laid this car park did me one favour without meaning to.

action: press 'y' -- northwest, third of eight
commentary: Two seconds that one, so I have crossed a painted line. Three down, five to go.

action: press 'y' -- northwest, fourth
commentary: Halfway. The wall is coming up on my left with its windows dark, and I can see the sidewalk running along the foot of it.

action: press 'y' -- northwest, fifth
commentary: Five. The door will be up on the left in three more if I have counted right, and I have counted right.

action: press 'y' -- northwest, sixth
commentary: There it is. The door standing black and open in the wall with the leaf swung back, four west and three north, and I can see the rubbish bin inside it and the racks beyond. Three more on the slant and one step west and I am under a roof again.

action: press 'y' -- northwest, seventh
commentary: Two more.

action: press 'y' -- northwest, eighth and last on the slant
commentary: One more and I am on the sidewalk level with the doorway.

action: press 'Left' -- step west into the doorway
commentary: Level with it. The leaf is swung back into the dark and the bin is just inside on the left. In I go.

action: press 'Left' -- one more west, clear of the threshold so I can shut it
commentary: Under a roof. That is the first time since I woke that there has been something over my head and I did not realise how much I minded until it was back.

action: press 'c' -- shut the door behind me
commentary: Now shut it. A door you leave open is an invitation and I have spent enough of my life being careful about what I let aboard.

action: press 'Up' -- north up the dark aisle for the green garment I promised myself
commentary: Shut. And the moment it shut the whole place went black as a hold with the hatch on. Dark suits me tonight. But before I settle I said I would come back for that green thing on the rack and it is one west and four north, so I am going to keep my word to myself. It is a habit worth keeping when there is nobody else left to keep one with.

action: press 'Up' -- north again, stepping past the bin
commentary: There is the bin under my boot, and it tells me getting over it is slow going. An empty bin in a golf shop. Somebody emptied it on the last normal Wednesday of the world and put the liner back in.

action: press 'Up' -- north, two more to the rack
commentary: Off the bin and it charged me for the privilege both ways. Two more.

action: press 'Up' -- north, level with the green garment
commentary: One more and it should be off my left shoulder.

action: press 'g' -- take the green garment off the rack
commentary: There it is, bright green in all this brown, hanging off the end of the rack at my left hand. Whatever it is, it is cloth, and cloth between my arms and a set of teeth is worth carrying.

action: press 'Escape' -- leave it on the rack, since I cannot carry it
commentary: Another golf bag. Green instead of brown, and it will not go anywhere on me because I am already wearing one exactly like it and there is no room left. So that was the promise kept and the reward was a second empty bag I cannot lift. That is fishing for you. You still shoot the net where you said you would.

action: press 'bar' -- settle here in the dark and let the day pass
commentary: So this is my station. Between the racks and the wall on the east side, which is the far side from whatever was gargling behind that northwest door, with one shut door between me and the car park and nothing else that opens on this side but glass. I have two handfuls of leaves I am not hungry enough for yet and a swamp written on a chart for the morning. There is nothing more to be got out of today that is worth the risk of going after it. So I sit down, and I let the light go.

action: press 'w' -- choose to wait rather than set the watch to wake me
commentary: It asks me whether I want to wait or set the alarm. My father's watch has an alarm on it and I have not used it since the morning of his funeral. Not yet. I will wait first and save the alarm for when I actually lie down.

action: press 'k' -- sit it out until dark
commentary: Eleven hours and fifty minutes until night. That is what I am choosing: all of it, in one sitting, back against the rack and the rod across my knees. It is not laziness. I have no water, no weapon worth the name and a back that has already told me twice today what it thinks of me, and the one thing I do have is a shut door and a dark corner. A skipper who goes out in weather she cannot handle does not get called brave. She gets called drowned.

action: press 'Y' -- stop the wait, because groaning is not a squirrel
commentary: Five and a half minutes of sitting still and then groaning. Not gargling this time. Groaning. That is a thing with lungs still trying to use them and it is close enough that I heard it through a wall with my eyes shut. Stop. Stop and listen and find out where before I decide anything else.

action: press 'bar' -- sit back down and start the wait again
commentary: Northwest. The same bearing as the gargling two hours ago, near enough, and I saw both of those doors standing shut with my own eyes when I came back in. So it is in a room it cannot get out of, or it is outside a wall it cannot get through, and either way it has had eight minutes to come at me and it has not. I am not walking toward it in the dark with a fishing rod. I am sitting back down.

action: press 'w' -- wait again rather than set the alarm
commentary: Wait, not alarm. The alarm is for tonight.

action: press 'k' -- till night again
commentary: Eleven hours and forty-four minutes of it left. Again.

action: press 'I' -- let the noise be and keep sitting, because I cannot flinch all day
commentary: Groaning, then whump, whump, whump, and now moaning. Something northwest is putting its shoulder into a door and the door is winning. Three times it has hit and three times it has not come through. Here is my decision and I will own it: I am not going to spend a whole day standing up every time that thing bumps into wood. I will let the noise be. If it ever gets through I will hear the wood go and that is a different sound entirely. Meanwhile the sun has found the window beside me and is warming my chest through the glass, and I am getting peckish, and both of those are better problems.

action: press 'I' -- ignore that too, because there is nothing in the world I can do about it
commentary: And there it is. Withdrawals. I have smoked since I was nineteen and I have had coffee in my hand every morning since I was twelve years old, and today is the day both of them come to collect. There is not a cigarette or a bean within reach of me and no amount of standing up will conjure one, so I will sit here and shake and let it pass. I knew what I was when I got out of bed. I am not going to be surprised by myself now.

action: press 'E' -- eat something before I lie down, such as it is
commentary: I sat there and did not move and did not touch a thing and let the whole day go past me, and it went. Sitting in the dark with my back against a rack, listening to something northwest put itself against a door over and over and never once get through. The light is gone now and I am very thirsty indeed. Not thirsty. Very thirsty, which is a different animal. So: eat, because there is nothing whatever to drink, and greens in the belly are better than nothing in the belly.

action: press 'Return' -- eat both handfuls now, because by morning they will be rotten
commentary: Thirteen calories. That is what my morning's foraging comes to: thirteen calories, a taste I will not enjoy, and a note that they are past their best and will be rotten inside nine hours. Thirteen. A slice of bread is eighty. But they will not keep until morning and I will not throw food away, so down they go, both handfuls, and I will pretend they were supper.

action: press 'I' -- ignore the craving and finish the mouthful
commentary: It is now interrupting my supper to inform me that I want a coffee. I am aware that I want a coffee. I have wanted a coffee since about eleven o'clock this morning and I will want one every hour until I find one or die, and neither of those things is going to happen in the next nine seconds, so let me eat my leaves.

action: press 'Return' -- eat the second handful as well, since it will be rotten by dawn
commentary: Thirteen calories eaten and the emptiness has gone out of my stomach, which tells you how empty it was. One handful left and it will be spoiled before the sun is up, so I will have that too. My mother would have called it a disgrace to a table. My mother never spent a night in a golf shop.

action: press 'bar' -- set the watch to wake me, the way I said I would; nothing on the screen changed
commentary: Right. Now the watch. He wore this thing every day from nineteen seventy-something until the morning he did not wake up, and I have never once set the alarm on it because I never needed telling when to get up. Tonight I need telling. I want to be awake and moving before the light is properly up, because there is a swamp five squares north with my name on it and I would rather cross a golf course at first light than at noon.

action: press 'I' -- answer the box the only way it will accept and finish the second handful
commentary: It wants Yes, No, a manager or an ignore, and nothing else. Twice I have handed it something else and twice it has taken no notice. Ignore, then, and let me finish my leaves.

action: press 'bar' -- reach for the watch now, to set it to wake me
commentary: Supper. Twenty-six calories of bitter leaves. Now the watch, because I want to be up and moving before the light is properly in the sky.

action: press 'dollar' -- give up on fiddling and simply lie down to sleep
commentary: Never mind, it says. Fine. I will not argue with it. I am going to lie down on a shop floor in the dark with my back against a rack, and if I am honest that is all I have wanted since about four o'clock.

action: press 'Y' -- say yes and lie down
commentary: Yes. Boots on, rod beside my hand, bag under my head for a pillow. Goodnight, Camille. Wherever you are in Salem, I hope you are somewhere with a door on it.

action: press '8' -- set the watch for eight hours, to wake at first light
commentary: There it is, offering after all. Eight hours. That puts me up at about four, which is when the sky starts going grey, and I want the whole of the light in front of me and none of it behind. First time I have ever set his alarm.

action: press 'I' -- ignore the craving again and stay lying down
commentary: It will not even let me fall asleep. That is what a habit is: it does not care that you are tired, it does not care that it is dark, it only wants what it wants. Ignore it. Stay down. Stay down, Odette.

action: press 'C' -- keep trying to sleep and stop being asked about it; nothing on the screen changed
commentary: Trouble sleeping. On a shop floor, thirsty, wanting tobacco, with something putting its weight on a door somewhere behind my head. Yes, I am having trouble sleeping. I am also fifty-two and I have been awake since eight this morning and I will get there. Keep trying, and stop asking me.

action: press 'I' -- ignore the craving once more and stay down
commentary: An hour and twenty minutes of sleep and it has woken me up to tell me about tobacco again. There is no tobacco. There will be no tobacco tomorrow either. Down.

action: press 'Escape' -- clear the notice and find out what woke me
commentary: Something woke me and then the world stopped to hand me a certificate for it. Survive for a day and find a safe place to sleep. A golf shop floor. Well. It was safe, which is more than most places managed.

action: press 'dollar' -- lie back down, because four hours is not a night
commentary: It was the groaning that woke me. Northwest, again, still at it in the small hours. Four hours is not a night and four in the morning is when I said I would be up, so I am going back down until the watch tells me otherwise. Hungry now as well as thirsty. Both of those keep.

action: press 'Y' -- yes, again
commentary: Yes. Same floor, same rack, same dark. Go back down.

action: press '4' -- set the watch for four hours, which lands on first light
commentary: Four hours this time. Four hours puts me at four in the morning, which is the hour I asked for in the first place and the hour the sky starts going grey over Rutland. Then up, and north, and see whether nine willows were telling me the truth.

action: press 'I' -- push the craving aside again and keep trying to sleep
commentary: And again. It has decided that the small hours are a good time to remind me what I have not got. Ignore. Sleep.

action: press 'C' -- keep trying to sleep and stop being asked
commentary: Twenty-five minutes of tossing and turning and it wants to know whether I would rather get up. No. I would rather sleep. Keep trying.

action: press 'S' -- wake to the watch and go straight for the save and quit
commentary: Beep-beep-beep. Thirty-four years that thing sat on his wrist and then nine on mine and this is the first time I have ever heard it do that. It worked. He would be unbearable about it. I am cold and I am dry to the bone and every part of me is a little weaker than it was yesterday, and I am getting up anyway, because the willows are north and I know it now.

action: press 'Y' -- answer yes and close the day out through the door the game keeps for it
commentary: One day. I woke up in a golf shop that had no water in it, I put a bag on my back, I looked into a car that will never move again, I got two handfuls of leaves out of the ground and thirteen calories out of one of them, and I found out where the water is. Nine willows and a word on a chart. That is not nothing. That is a day's work, and my father would have called it a fair one. North, when I have had a moment. Camille, if you are reading anything anywhere, your mother is still here.
